# auth-session

Session handling for the admin console.

- `server/` — Express + TypeScript. Token issuing in `server/auth/`, routes in `server/routes/`.
- `client/` — React + TypeScript. Session state in `client/src/auth/`.

Access tokens are short-lived; the client refreshes them before expiry.

report:
1. Every token is rejected as expired the moment it is issued — nobody can stay signed in.
2. Signing in with a wrong password still succeeds and returns a token.
3. After navigating away from a page that uses auto-refresh, the refresh keeps firing forever; opening and
   closing that screen a few times results in several refreshes per cycle.
4. If the login request fails, the screen shows nothing at all — no message, and the user is left staring at
   the form wondering whether it worked.
5. Reloading the browser tab signs the user out, even though the session was saved.

bugs.label: token expiry compares seconds against milliseconds
login failure never surfaced to the user
saved session never restored on load

precise:
Make exactly these five changes.

1. `server/auth/tokens.ts`, `verifyToken` — `payload.exp` is stored in SECONDS since the epoch, but it is compared
   against `Date.now()`, which is MILLISECONDS. Every token therefore looks already expired. Compare both sides in
   the same unit.

2. `server/routes/session.ts`, `POST /session` — the handler checks only that `password` is non-empty and then
   issues a token, so any password succeeds. Reject an incorrect password with HTTP 401. There is no user store in
   this codebase; introduce a single explicit expected value and compare against it.

3. `client/src/auth/useAutoRefresh.ts` — the `setInterval` created in `useEffect` is never cleared, so each mount
   leaves another timer running forever. Clear it when the effect is torn down.

4. `client/src/components/LoginForm.tsx` — `submit` never checks `res.ok` and never sets the `error` state that is
   already declared and already rendered, so a failed login shows the user nothing. Set that error state when the
   request fails.

5. `client/src/auth/session.ts` — `setSession` writes to `localStorage`, but nothing ever reads it back, so the
   in-memory `current` starts as `null` after a page reload and the user appears signed out. Restore the persisted
   session on load.
